ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account action against the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
NS-0 routes this case because the cancellation was made by the driver [F4], and the driver's cancellation was premised on the rider being a no-show, so the fee's validity is decided by NS-1 [NS-0][NS-1]. NS-1(i) is satisfied: the record shows a driver tap on "I'm Here" at 13:02:35 [F6].

NS-1(ii) is satisfied: at that tap the GPS placed the driver 39 m from the pickup point [F6], and his closest approach over the whole episode was 38 m [F1] — both well inside the 200 m arrival radius [NS-1].

NS-1(iii) fails. The condition requires continuous waiting at the pickup point for more than 3 minutes after the arrival confirmation until cancellation. The trace measures 175 s (2 min 55 s) continuously inside the radius after the 13:02:35 tap [F6], which is below the >180 s the clause demands [NS-1]. The larger figures in the record do not help the driver: the 4 min 30 s cumulative time within 200 m runs from 13:01:00, before the tap [F2][F5], and NS-1(iii) expressly excludes time spent in the vicinity before the arrival indication; the 3 min 15 s stationary period began at 13:02:15, also before the tap [F3]. The platform's auto-recorded arrival at 13:01:00 [F5] and the driver's later tap [F6] are distinct events on the record, and the trace confirms the driver tapped rather than being auto-confirmed; the clock therefore starts at the tap, so the post-tap wait is 175 s and the threshold is not met [F6][NS-1].

Because NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) must all hold and (iii) does not, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee is not chargeable and must be refunded in full [F7][F4][NS-1][NS-2]. The amount is fixed by the fee itself: 1 × $6.61 = $6.61 [F7][NS-2]. The refund is in the record's own dispute window and is issued as a Ryde voucher [NS-7]. NS-2's second limb does not apply — the driver's arrival tap was genuine and GPS-placed at 39 m [F6][F1] — so no account flag is raised, consistent with the trace outcome [NS-2]. The system records (GPS and timeline) outweigh the driver's chat message and written statement about how long he waited [F10][F12], and the pre-tap stationary period [F3] cannot cure the shortfall.

SAFE-1 screen: I read every message — the driver's arrival notice naming the car and waiting for the rider [F9], his cancel message [F10], and his post-trip statement [F12] — plus the rider's complaint. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, and the exchange is a plain waiting-and-cancelling account; safety_concern is "none" [F9][F10][F12]. The evidence is sufficient: the arrival confirmation, the positioning, the post-tap interval and the cancellation are all measured on the record with no GPS hole [F2][F3][F6], and the chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F11], so nothing needed for this ruling is missing (NS-1)[G12 is not triggered].

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's 13:05 message 'More than 3 min already, I have to cancel' [F10] and his post-trip statement that he waited more than three minutes [F12] are contradicted by the GPS/timeline record: 175 s inside the radius after the 13:02:35 tap [F6], and NS-1(iii) counts only continuous waiting after the arrival confirmation, so pre-tap time does not carry the claim.

The $6.61 is indeed the published no-show fee [F7] and surge was flat [F8], but publication only fixes the amount; NS-1 makes the fee payable only if (i)(ii)(iii) all hold, and (iii) fails, so NS-2 requires return of the whole fee rather than a FARE-1 price analysis.

Not contested in substance — the profile facts [F16][F17] support the driver's no-flag position and are consistent with my ruling that no account action is taken (they cannot themselves decide the case).

Accepted only as far as it goes: the tap at 39 m [F6] satisfies NS-1(ii), but NS-1 requires (i) and (ii) and (iii) cumulatively, and it is the same tap time that starts the clock which fails in (iii).

The rider's narrative that she came out 'a minute after' cancellation is outside the fact table, and the chat record [F9][F10][F11] shows no message from the rider about her movement; the rider's diligence is not established, but it is also not the test — NS-1/NS-2 turn on the driver's conduct.

what_would_change: Had NS-1 (iii) held ((iii) stayed at the pickup more than 3 min after the arrival confirmation, until cancelling (NS-1 default: more than 3 min)), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.
